name: Trajectory
summary: Trajectory is a San Francisco research and product lab building AI systems designed for continual learning from real-world feedback.
overview: Trajectory is a research and product lab building continual-learning infrastructure for AI products. It uses production signals to identify where models succeed or fail, then helps teams post-train models using that real-world feedback.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Company site identifies a $15M seed; valuation was not disclosed.

bull_case: A dependable feedback loop between production usage and post-training could become essential infrastructure as companies move from static models to continuously improving AI products.
bear_case: Continual learning carries technical, data-governance and evaluation challenges. The company has not publicly disclosed a financing or valuation, so commercial maturity remains hard to assess.
directory_notes: Public financing and operating data remain limited.

intelligence.description: Continual-learning platform that turns production signals into ongoing improvement for AI systems.
company: Trajectory is building continual-learning infrastructure for AI products. It analyzes production interactions to surface where a system succeeds or fails, then helps teams use those signals to post-train models for their specific products.

The company describes itself as both a research lab and product lab. Public financing and valuation details remain undisclosed, so the profile focuses on its technology and avoids an inferred transaction.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Many AI products are limited by the gap between a base model and real-world usage. If Trajectory can close that loop safely and reliably, it addresses a foundational problem for companies building differentiated AI applications.

changed.text: Trajectory identifies a $15M seed and describes its continual-learning platform on its public site.

takeaways: Trajectory turns production signals into feedback for AI post-training.
The company is building a continual-learning platform rather than a standalone consumer model.
The company identifies a $15M seed; a valuation was not disclosed.
